chunks: 4 - Abul Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Katib reported to me from al-Hasan ibn Abdul Karim al-Za'farani, from Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Warraq, from Abdullah ibn al-Azraq al-Shaybani, from Abu al-Jahhaf, from Mu'awiyah ibn Tha'labah who said:

When Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan's rule was firmly established, he dispatched Busr ibn Artat to Hejaz to hunt for the followers of the Commander of the Believers Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him. At that time, Ubaidullah ibn al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib governed Makkah. Busr summoned him but could not find him. He was then informed that Ubaidullah had two infant sons. He searched for them, found them, seized them and brought them out from where they were hiding. They had two tender forelocks like pearls. He ordered their slaughter. When the news reached their mother, she nearly died of grief. Then she recited:

'Alas! Who has heard of my two sons, who were like two pearls torn from their shell! Alas! Who has heard of my two sons, they were my ears and my eyes, and my heart today is wrenched! I was told of Busr, but I could not believe what they claimed, from their words and the falsehood they contrived. The sharp, honed sword fell upon the throats of my two little ones — such is tyranny and immoderation. Who will show compassion to a grief-stricken, weeping, bereaved mother for two infants who perished after their forebears departed.'

Then Ubaidullah ibn al-Abbas and Busr ibn Artat later met in the presence of Mu'awiyah. Mu'awiyah said to Ubaidullah: 'Do you recognize this old man, the killer of the two infants?' Busr said: 'Yes, I killed them — so what?' Ubaidullah said: 'If only I had a sword!' Busr said: 'Here, take my sword,' pointing to his sword. Mu'awiyah scolded and rebuked him saying: 'Woe to you, old man! How foolish you are! You go to a man whose two sons you killed and offer him your sword? As if you don't know the courage of the sons of Hashim! By Allah, had you given it to him, he would have killed you first and then me.' Ubaidullah said: 'On the contrary, by Allah, I would have started with you and then followed with him.'

key_terms.بسر بن أرطاة: Busr ibn Artat, a military commander loyal to Mu'awiyah, notorious for his brutality against supporters of Ali (AS)
key_terms.بني هاشم: Banu Hashim, the noble clan of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) and his family, known for their bravery
key_terms.شيعة أمير المؤمنين: Followers/partisans of the Commander of the Believers Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS)

ai.seo_question: What happened to the sons of Ubaidullah ibn al-Abbas during Mu'awiyah's persecution of Imam Ali's followers?
ai.summary: This narrative recounts the brutal killing of the two infant sons of Ubaidullah ibn al-Abbas by Busr ibn Artat, an agent of Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan sent to Hejaz to persecute the supporters of Imam Ali (AS). The mother's poignant elegy and the later confrontation between Ubaidullah and Busr in Mu'awiyah's presence reveal the depth of Hashimite courage and the callousness of Umayyad persecution, with Ubaidullah boldly declaring he would have killed Mu'awiyah first if given a sword.
